newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wool prices slightly weaker in week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wool prices slightly weaker in week.

text.p: Australian wool prices were slightly weaker at sales this week in Melbourne, Newcastle and Fremantle, pastorol group Wesfarmers Dalgety said.

The eastern market indicator fell six cent to 570 cents a kg clean, while the western market indicator fell three cents to 532 cents a kg. A total of 85,259 bales were offered, with a pass-in rate of 9.4 percent.

"Demand conditions remain unchanged. Many processors are still operating on a hand to mouth basis, with purchases simply at a level to keep machinery running," the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.

Wesfarmers said that as predicted, very high prices were paid this week for stylish, good quality, superfine wools. Strong demand from European interests, particularly Italian, added to the steadily improving buyer sentiment, it said.
Wool International sold 5,959 bales and the stockpile now stands at 2,030,628 bales.
In the futures market, a total of 209 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract in the week ended November 7.
Sales next week are in Sydney, Adelaide and Fremantle with a total of about 115,561 bales on offer.
